notes: Modified cash basis school district; no business-type funds (school lunch is a governmental fund), so business_type and reported_totals.business-type are null. Basic-statement lines come from the Total Governmental Funds column (p6) of the Statement of Receipts, Expenditures and Changes in Fund Balances, which is net of the Reclassifications column (interfund transfers and payments eliminated), so no transfers appear in the total column and transfers_in/out are null. Beginning/ending 'cash' = the fund balance/net position the statement rolls forward (298,019,370 -> 363,680,615), which includes investments (379,729,539, p4), inventories and is net of accrued expenses/encumbrances; actual cash is only 220,382. Identity: 298,019,370 + 739,730,743 - 674,069,498 = 363,680,615. Balance sheet is the Statement of Net Position (governmental activities column; the only column). Detail: General Fund uses the budget-and-actual schedule (pp7-10; most detailed; expenditures are by function code so detail_category is not itemized). The printed General Fund total expenditures 578,567,384 includes all transfers out of 26,227,871 per the p22 fund summary (expenditures 552,339,513 + transfers out 26,227,871): the 8000 line 726,762 is shown as other financing, and the other 25,501,109 (to Depreciation 13,503,467, Contingency 9,814,056, Cooperative 2,183,586) sits inside the function-line spending. In addition 6,648,493 of General Fund payments to ESU 18 sits inside General Fund spending and inside ESU 18 'Contracted services' revenue; p6 eliminates it, so it is treated as a transfer: General Fund other financing -6,648,493 and ESU 18 other financing +6,648,493 (Contracted services 7,480,305 split into 831,812 revenue plus the 6,648,493 transfer in; ESU printed revenue total includes other financing). The General Fund contra expenditure is widened to a total of -32,149,602 (25,501,109 + 6,648,493), allocated by function per the p6 Reclassifications column: -5,044,139 instruction (Instruction 4,649,139 + Categorical corporation and private 395,000), -25,401,169 support services (Instruction 1,473,679 + General administration 7,763,016 + Central services 6,939,464 + Operation and maintenance 9,225,010) and -1,704,294 student transportation (specific schedule lines not identifiable on the pages); General Fund other financing lines sum to -32,876,364 (-26,227,871 transfers out plus -6,648,493... see items) and expenditure items then sum to 545,691,020. Detail revenue and spending then equal the p6 totals 739,730,743 and 674,069,498 across funds. ESU 18 'Co-op contracts' 4,293,118 is eliminated as a transfer on p6, so it is recorded as ESU other financing -4,293,118 (not spending) and Cooperative Member Payments 4,527,961 is split into 234,843 revenue and a 4,293,118 transfer in (other financing); the ESU printed expenditure total and Cooperative printed revenue total are unchanged. Federal programs, categorical programs and ESU 18 other lines have function guessed. The 3551 Career Education actual is 253,697 (variance column confirms). Other funds' budget schedules pp12-20 and ESU 18 actuals p23 recorded line by line; lines with a dash actual are 0 or omitted (bond refunding proceeds/escrow payment lines on p14 are dashes and omitted). The p22 fund summary (excluding ESU 18) is a summary and not recorded as detail; p21 is a note. Fund-level detail uses schedule amounts, which differ from the statement columns where interfund transfers are included (e.g. GF schedule receipts include county/other items; ESU 18 shown separately). Depreciation Fund has only one expenditure line, so no expenditure total is recorded; School Lunch has one expenditure line and no printed total; Student Fees has one revenue line. Informational, not recorded (the schedules exclude it from fund balance; not receipts or spending): Cash at County Treasurer (Lancaster County) General Fund 9,385,978 (p11), Bond Fund 983,249 (p14), QCPU Fund 105,259 (p15), ESU 18 141,226 (p23). Contingency Fund insurance/workers compensation lines are support services (school business services). Read pages 1-23 of 23.
